title: Annual burned area, all land cover types, Argentina, 2002 to 2025 (GWIS, from the MODIS MCD64A1 burned-area product)
source: Global Wildfire Information System (GWIS, European Commission Joint Research Centre / Copernicus), country profile statistics, "Global Yearly Burned Area by Land Cover Type", as redistributed by Our World in Data (2026), chart "Annual area burnt by wildfires" (indicator 1357121, "Yearly burned area across all land types – GWIS (MODIS)", minor processing by OWID, dataset version 2026-11-11). Underlying product: NASA MODIS MCD64A1 burned area.
originalPublisher: https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/apps/country.profile/downloads (data fetched by OWID via the GWIS country profile API, cprof.effis.emergency.copernicus.eu)
licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/about-gwis/data-license, as stated in the OWID metadata)
retrievalNote: Downloaded with curl on 2026-11-15 (America/Toronto evening; the OWID metadata file stamps dateDownloaded 2026-11-16 in UTC). Raw files: data/official/raw/argentina_gwis_owid_annual-area-burnt-by-wildfires-gwis_ARG.csv (values copied verbatim, national total as published, no summing), argentina_gwis_owid_chart-metadata.json, argentina_gwis_owid_indicator-1357121-metadata.json. Not fetched directly from GWIS tonight: the country-profile API is undocumented and a probe returned HTTP 500, so the values are as redistributed by OWID (minor processing). The Climatic Research Unit series below, computed independently from the same MCD64A1 product, moves with it year by year (see scripts/check_argentina_official.mjs).
notes: NOT an official national statistic: a satellite burned-area estimate. GWIS country statistics are built from fire events mapped by the MODIS MCD64A1 burned-area product (surface-reflectance change, 500 m), so the series is independent of VIIRS and has no sensor change in 2012, but it is NOT independent of MODIS: it uses the same Terra/Aqua instruments, and the MCD64A1 algorithm also uses the 1 km MODIS active-fire observations to guide its classification (LP DAAC product description: 500 m surface reflectance coupled with 1 km MODIS active fire observations). It therefore checks that a record without a sensor switch shows no post-2012 rise; it is not a ground-truth check like the Canadian National Forestry Database, and agreement with the harmonized series is partly expected because both are MODIS-scaled. One method for the whole period 2002-2025 (no change in 2012). MCD64A1 misses small and cloud- or canopy-obscured fires and is known to underestimate burned area; agricultural burning of small plots is under-represented. The 2025 value is the latest release and may be revised. A second MCD64A1-based country series (Climatic Research Unit global fire dashboard, MCD64A1 C6.1, units as published, 2001-2023) is kept below as a cross-check of processing only: it is the same satellite product, not a second independent source; its 2023 value is clearly incomplete (38 vs 101-275 in other years) and is excluded. Argentina's national fire statistics (Servicio Nacional de Manejo del Fuego, provincial reports compiled by the Ministry) could not be used for a 2003-2011 vs 2012+ comparison tonight: the open-data file of reported area by jurisdiction (CIAM dt_id 416) starts in 2017 and has provinces without data (s/d) in several years; earlier years exist only as yearly PDF reports. The Ministry's native-forest-only series (CIAM dt_id 382, 1993-2023) is kept as a secondary series: it covers native forest only, its method is not documented in the dataset metadata, and its 2003-2011 mean is dominated by 2003.

cru_mcd64a1.title: Total burned area by country, yearly, Argentina (BA_Total), Climatic Research Unit global fire dashboard (MODIS MCD64A1 Collection 6.1)
cru_mcd64a1.units: as published (column "sum"; the dashboard labels country totals in thousands of km²; only ratios are used here)
cru_mcd64a1.use: 2003-2022 only (2023 incomplete in the file). Same satellite product as the main series: a processing cross-check, not independent evidence.
